text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
All newspapers lead with Cambodia fighting, with Second Prime Minister Hun Sen in control of Phnom Penh.
-- Most of the Malaysians caught in the fighting in Phnom Penh have already been successfully relocated to designated safe havens by the Malaysian embassy in Phnom Penh.

-- Despite continuous efforts to liberalise the country's financial sector, the government will continue to keep a close watch on it to ensure the freedom is not abused, acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Monday.

-- Auditors and auditing companies are not cooperating with the Registrar of Companies' nationwide accounts and auditing operation since it started in February, Domestic Trade and Consumer Affairs Minister Megat Junid Megat Ayob said.
-- RHB Capital, already the largest fully integrated financial services group in Malaysia, is poised to become the country's first homegrown, multinational financial institution.

-- Malaysia has called on the two contending factions in Cambodia to end all hostilities and seek a peaceful resolution to their conflict, and to ensure the safety of all foreign nationals in the country.
